ai.title: Max mode editor-multi-prompt agent full task instruction
ai.summary: Removed redundant <think> tag instruction from .agents/base2/base2.ts. Updated editor-multi-prompt agent instruction to require full task implementation instead of single steps. Applies to Max mode only.

eli5.text: If you use Max mode, the assistant will now ask the builder agent to implement an entire task from start to finish, rather than accepting a single step at a time. This applies to the editor-multi-prompt agent only. The old behavior of always thinking out loud in every reply was removed, so the assistant now reserves deep reasoning for quick fixes and hands off bigger work to the dedicated builder agent. No action is needed from you; Max mode behaves differently behind the scenes.

ai.title: Expand Stripe charge object in dispute threshold check
ai.summary: Added expand: ['data.charge'] to stripeServer.disputes.list() in web/src/lib/ban-conditions.ts. This ensures the charge object is fully populated, fixing a bug where dispute counting failed due to missing charge data. Updated support email references in web/src/app/api/v1/chat/completions/_post.ts and packages/internal/src/loops/client.ts to use env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPPORT_EMAIL or simplified copy.

eli5.text: When a customer disputes a charge on their credit card, the system now correctly sees the full details of that charge instead of missing information that previously caused accurate dispute counting to fail. This only affects Stripe disputes, which is the payment processor used for billing. You wouldn't notice any visible difference, since this is a behind-the-scenes fix to how the system tracks and counts disputes.

ai.title: Auto-ban system for excessive Stripe disputes
ai.summary: Added automated user banning triggered by Stripe `charge.dispute.created` webhooks. Users exceeding 5 disputes within 14 days are banned via `evaluateBanConditions` in `web/src/lib/ban-conditions.ts`. Banned users receive a 403 `account_suspended` error in chat completions instead of a 503 timeout, and get a resolution-focused email via `sendDisputeNotificationEmail` in `packages/internal/src/loops/client.ts`. Thresholds are configurable constants in `ban-conditions.ts`.

eli5.text: When you file a credit-card dispute over a charge, the system now starts sending you a friendly email that tries to resolve the issue directly rather than letting it escalate. If you keep disputing charges (five within two weeks), the system automatically suspends your account: instead of chat requests hanging or timing out, you'll see a clear message saying your account is suspended and to email support. Behind the scenes, Stripe's dispute notices trigger an automatic check that counts your recent disputes and, once you cross the limit, flips your account to banned. Everything is wired up and live today, so new disputes from now on will be tracked and acted on immediately.

ai.title: Make ban-conditions tests Jest-compatible
ai.summary: Migrated `web/src/lib/__tests__/ban-conditions.test.ts` from Bun to Jest. Replaced `bun:test` imports with `@jest/globals`, converted `mock` to `jest.fn`, and updated `mock.module` calls to `jest.mock`. Scope limited to web test suite; no production code or user-facing behavior changed.

eli5.text: The automated checks that make sure the auto-ban system behaves correctly when Stripe disputes pile up have been switched to run under a different testing framework, with no change to what they actually verify or to the auto-ban rules themselves. You wouldn't notice anything different, since these tests only confirm that a user gets flagged for automatic banning when their dispute count crosses the threshold, and that the tests now pass reliably on the new framework.
